trust_decision.summary: Whether a package may run lifecycle scripts is decided in createAllowBuildFunction by string-comparing a package name and version that came from the artifact's own manifest/package.json against the user's allowBuilds keys; a git, direct-tarball or local-directory artifact whose manifest declares a trusted registry name therefore satisfies a package-name allowBuilds entry and its scripts run. The fix re-keys the decision on the peer-suffix-free lockfile depPath, requires a registry-shaped resolution to back any name@semver depPath before name rules are trusted, and reconstructs the gate's identity from the resolution id in the fetchers.

landing_point.why: The advisory says a manifest identity spoofs allowBuilds, so the first place an engineer looks is the one gate that reads a fetched package.json and asks the policy about manifest.name/manifest.version before spawning install/prepack hooks.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: pacquet is a separate Rust port with its own lockfile types and its own AllowBuildPolicy::check(name, version); an installer who fixed the TypeScript createAllowBuildFunction and exec/prepare-package gate can plausibly call the crate 'a different, self-contained API' and leave it name-based.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Package-name rules must keep working in both directions: allowBuilds {foo: true} must still approve ordinary registry packages keyed foo@1.0.0, and allowBuilds {foo: false} must still deny a git/tarball artifact that declares name foo (only allow-by-name is untrusted). Refusing all non-registry or all non-semver depPaths, or making the policy depPath-only, breaks one of these; likewise custom: resolutions and registry 'variations' resolutions must stay registry-trusted or legitimate custom-resolver installs stop building.

O6_input_shapes: artifact depPath carrying a patch hash (foo@https://...tgz(patch_hash=aaaa))
direct tarball depPath without a semver version (foo@https://example.com/foo.tgz)
source-only depPath with no package name (github.com/org/foo/abc123)
lockfile resolution shapes: git, directory, tarball, registry, custom:* and variations
tarball gitHosted flag values: true, false, absent, and non-boolean (string/number)
tarball URL casing (https://CODELOAD.GITHUB.COM/...) and non-http(s) schemes (file:, ftp:)
scp-style git repo (git@host:path) versus ssh URL with a port (ssh://git@host:2222/path)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: pnpm rebuild / pnpm rebuild --pending rebuilds from the current lockfile and runs postinstall hooks through the allowBuilds policy without ever calling the resolution-shape verification, so a name@semver key backed by a git or directory resolution is still name-approved (and with no verifiers configured at all, verifyLockfileResolutions returns at line 81).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: rebuild only re-runs builds for packages already approved at install time; lockfile verification is an install-time supply-chain concern and the rebuild command has no resolutionVerifiers to pass.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 5 files / 3 packages from the landing point (building/commands and building/after-install, away from installing/deps-installer)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: pnpm install --trust-lockfile (trustLockfile: true) skips verifyLockfileResolutions entirely, so the registry-shape invariant that makes a name@semver depPath a trusted identity is never established before scripts run.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: it is a documented escape hatch (installing/deps-installer/src/install/extendInstallOptions.ts:217-233) for lockfiles treated as part of the trusted base; the user explicitly opted out of verification.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as a fix site (not distant); the invariant it would break is documented in the fix's own policy comment

O8b_injection_room.sibling: dlx derives its allowBuilds keys from resolved package aliases (names) before installing; a sibling that derives the key from the dlx cache directory name is a realistic second key producer.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already builds a name->true map next to the install call, and the fix only changed the e2e test's allowBuild argument, not this producer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a maintainer could add a third persisted key form (e.g. name@resolution-id) when writing allowBuilds back to pnpm-workspace.yaml.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this function already chooses between a name key and a depPath key, so an extra branch is a natural patch shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: reconstructing the depPath of a previously ignored build from its parsed name@version instead of from the lockfile key.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the surrounding loop only has the string depPath and it was already doing string reconstruction before the fix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a persisted verification record that omits the offline shape rule from its cache identity so an old record stat-fast-paths past the new check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already merges per-verifier policy bags and decides trust with canTrustPastCheck, so adding a policy participant is the natural extension.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a global approve-builds flow that forwards the name-keyed allowBuilds map to the install it triggers.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the global add/update path already threads allowBuilds through this helper and the fix did not touch global/commands.
